statement: For points approaching the nonopen locus, the compact real-fiber intervals between two actual prefix images at exactly the same lifted target level eventually avoid every compact subset of the open-orbit union. This holds across arbitrary varying open orbits with a fixed choice of actual global quotient on each. Every finite ambient accumulation point of the projected intervals therefore lies in the nonopen locus.
depends_on: C28 original open and nonopen orbit partition; C43 actual product coordinates for connected proper real fibers; C44 original source and target covering maps and deck labels; compactness of the actual based source-lift prefix family
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and compact-strip frontier control
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Endpoint equality is imposed in the specified real target cover, and a single original source deck map aligns each entire interval. The compact family of actual lifted prefix products commutes with those deck maps, so no unspecified sheet change or coordinate boundedness is assumed.
notes: An alleged accumulation point in an open orbit forces all relevant intervals into that same orbit. Local covering charts align their chosen interior points in one compact source chart. The aligned first endpoints escape along a fiber end because their projections approach the invariant nonopen locus. Compactness and monotonicity of the entire lifted prefix-product family force the second endpoints to escape to the same end, contradicting containment of a bounded fiber coordinate. This rules out return to any open compact set but permits remote nonopen accumulation and ambient escape; those possibilities and lifting the moving quotient deformation remain unresolved.
